summary: White wooden light above Chute Cove on the Bay of Fundy, built 1911; owned since 2001 by a local historical society.

access.note: Grounds and tower open on weekend afternoons in summer, per the society (Lighthouse Friends).

events.note: Built November 1911 by Joseph Marshall, on land bought from Lloyd Brooks.
Kerosene lamp, lit each night at sunset and extinguished at daybreak; sixth-order dioptric lens.
Electrified in the 1940s; the sources do not give the exact year.
Coast Guard re-shingled the sides and repaired the lantern, February to May 1993.
Passed from the federal government (DFO) to the Hampton Lighthouse Society for $1; agreement signed 30 November 2001.

keepers.name: Tom Burton
keepers.note: Named by the Preservation Society as the first light keeper, for a short period before Herbert Foster took over. No dates given in the source.

keepers.name: Herbert Foster
keepers.note: First keeper according to Lighthouse Friends; annual salary $180; looked after the light until at least 1923. The 1913 Department statement names "H. Foster" against Hampton, appointed 2 Dec 1911 at $180 (read from the page image, scan p. 68, printed p. 61); the matching salary is the basis for treating the two as the same man. The Preservation Society names Tom Burton as first keeper.

keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends gives the 1920s to the 1950s.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: All sources (Register, Lighthouse Friends, NSLPS and the 1912 Department report) give 1911 for the tower, and the 1912 Department report records the tower's construction under the fiscal year ended 31 March 1912, which fits a November 1911 completion. The Department's 1900 wharfinger table also lists a 'Judson Foster' at Hampton from 1888; that table lists wharfingers, not lightkeepers, so it is not treated as a lighthouse keeper.
NSLPS writes 'John Titus' for the contract; Lighthouse Friends and the Department report give J. F. Titus of Hampton. The story uses J. F. Titus.

Lighthouse Friends names Herbert Foster as the first keeper; the Preservation Society names Tom Burton as the first keeper for a short period before Foster. The story states both. The 1913 statement gives "H. Foster" at Hampton, appointed 2 December 1911 at $180, which matches Lighthouse Friends' salary for Foster.

corrections.proposed: Hampton Lighthouse and Historical Society (non-profit; transferred from DFO in 2001)
corrections.why: The Register, Lighthouse Friends and NSLPS all record the transfer of ownership to the society.
Owner now runs the light as a community lighthouse; the Coast Guard still lists the light.

notes_for_editor: Two OCR table readings are matched by column position and need a human look against the page image: (1) the 1912 works table (scan p. 49), where 'J. F. Titus, Hampton' is matched to the Hampton tower row by position, consistent with Lighthouse Friends' $585 contract; the expenditure figures in the same OCR block were not used; (2) the 1912 statement of light stations (scan p. 68, printed p. 61), where 'H. Foster' is the first name in the lightkeeper column beside Hampton, consistent with Lighthouse Friends' Herbert Foster (1911 to at least 1923). Keeper dates after 1923 rest on Lighthouse Friends alone. The 1900 wharfinger table (Judson Foster at Hampton, 1888) is a table of wharfs, not lights, and is not used. Opening hours and the open-tower status come from Lighthouse Friends and may be dated: check with the society before relying on them. The Register description says 'Chute Bay' once; the Coast Guard list and the other sources say Chute Cove. No newspaper search was run for Hampton (no free Canadian newspaper archive was found; Chronicling America is US-only). No storm, wreck or rescue tied to the station turned up in the sources read, so there is no storms chapter. The record's wood structure type and 10.1 m height come from Lighthouse Friends and Wikidata. Chapter count: five headings (The place, Building the light, The keepers, After the keepers, Today), each with sourced material, which is above the 2 to 4 chapter shape of a moderate story; the editor may trim. Fact-check 2026-10-27: both OCR table readings were checked against the page images. Scan p. 49 (printed p. 42) shows "J. F. Titus, Hampton" on the Hampton tower row, contract $585.00, with inspection fees and site $88.97; scan p. 68 (printed p. 61) shows "H. Foster" at Hampton, appointed Dec. 2, 1911, salary $180.00. The story sets out the disagreements about the first keeper (Burton, per NSLPS), the contractor name (John Titus, per NSLPS) and the present light (NSLPS gives fixed white and "Still Operating: No"; the Coast Guard list gives a red flash). The "what hazard the light was first meant to mark" gap, which the story no longer states, is a research limit: no source read gives it.
